name: afalg-then-splice
why: socket(AF_ALG) (a0=0x26, SOCK_SEQPACKET) followed by splice() in the same pid within 5s is the CopyFail syscall correlation
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for copyfail_behavioral.c (same-pid AF_ALG socket + splice(pipe->op_fd)); splice a1/a3 are the NULL off_in/off_out, exit is the decimal byte count

name: afalg-then-splice-window-edge
why: the same AF_ALG+splice pair 4s apart stays inside the 5s window; the correlation must still fire at the window edge
source: synthetic: a slower exploit, AF_ALG socket and splice 4s apart in one pid

name: cryptsetup-afalg-no-splice
why: cryptsetup opens an AF_ALG SOCK_SEQPACKET socket for LUKS keyslot decryption via the kernel crypto API and drives it with sendmsg/read, never splice; half the correlation, so the splice base must be required. (libkcapi's hash tools do splice; the AF_ALG base filters them, see kcapi-hasher-large-file-filtered.)
source: recorded via source: cryptsetup lib/crypto_backend/crypto_cipher_kernel.c:62 socket(AF_ALG, SOCK_SEQPACKET, 0); no splice in the crypto backend

name: inet-socket-then-splice
why: an AF_INET (a0=2) socket plus splice() keeps both the socket() and splice() surface but is not the AF_ALG family; the a0=0x26 constraint inside the socket base must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: a proxy opening a TCP socket then splicing for zero-copy

name: afalg-and-splice-different-pid
why: the AF_ALG socket in one pid and splice() in another within 5s split the halves across processes; the pid group-by must enforce same-process
source: synthetic: AF_ALG socket in pid X, splice in unrelated pid Y

name: afalg-then-splice-too-late
why: the same pid opens an AF_ALG socket and splices 30s later, outside the 5s window; the timespan must bound the correlation
source: synthetic: a long-lived crypto daemon that splices unrelated data much later

name: kcapi-hasher-large-file-filtered
why: kcapi-hasher run as sha256hmac on a file of 32 KiB or more (libkcapi lib/kcapi-md.c splices any update with len >= 1<<15): libkcapi opens socket(AF_ALG, SOCK_SEQPACKET), creates its pipe at handle init, and vmsplice()s then splice()s the input into the op fd within milliseconds -- the rule's exact sequence. The kcapi_hash_tools filter on the AF_ALG base suppresses it (the old rule fired on it)
source: libkcapi lib/kcapi-kernel-if.c (_kcapi_common_vmsplice_iov: vmsplice then splice(handle->pipes[0] -> op fd)); Makefile.am hasher_links symlink sha256hmac to bindir/kcapi-hasher

name: kcapi-enc-afalg-splice-still-fires
why: kcapi-enc runs AEAD ciphers (authencesn among them) through the same vmsplice/splice path, so it can perform the CopyFail write; it is not filtered and must still fire

name: hasher-name-from-tmp-still-fires
why: an exploit that names itself sha256sum with prctl still fires: the hash-tool entries need the libkcapi binary as well as the name
source: synthetic: prctl(PR_SET_NAME, "sha256sum") then socket(AF_ALG) and splice from /tmp/cf

name: ldpreload-into-kcapi-hasher-known-miss
why: KNOWN MISS (a CopyFail sequence that the kcapi_hash_tools filter suppresses): an unprivileged user runs kcapi-hasher, a non-setuid, dynamically linked binary, as sha256sum with LD_PRELOAD. The injected code opens socket(AF_ALG, SOCK_SEQPACKET), binds it to authencesn (auditd does not record the cipher name), creates a pipe and splices, all in the tool's pid with its comm and exe, so the AF_ALG base filter alone suppresses the correlation. It differs from the tool's own large-file hash only in the uid (1000 here; the event schema does not carry it) and in the cipher name. Labelled filtered because that is what the rule does with it today; if the filter is tightened, this case fires and becomes a positive
source: synthetic from recorded mechanism: LD_PRELOAD into a non-setuid binary keeps its comm and exe (recorded on this host for /usr/bin/gdb and /usr/bin/runc as uid 65534); event shape as kcapi-hasher-large-file-filtered with the uid and auid of an unprivileged user
